turns.reply:

The Central Bank of Nigeria introduced it in 2014 to reduce fraud and identity theft in the banking system. Your BVN links all your bank accounts together, so banks can verify it's really you when you open an account or do certain transactions.

You enroll once at any bank by providing your fingerprints, facial photograph, and other personal details. The same BVN then works for every bank account you have.

**Airtime (or call credit)** is what you use for voice calls and SMS text messages. You can also use it to pay for data bundles or other services, but by itself, it doesn't connect you to the internet.

**Data** is specifically for internet access—browsing, streaming, downloading, using apps like WhatsApp, Instagram, YouTube, etc. You buy data in bundles (daily, weekly, monthly plans) measured in megabytes (MB) or gigabytes (GB).

In short: airtime is for calls and texts; data is for the internet. You can sometimes convert airtime to data by buying a bundle, but you can't use data for calls.

>
> The Bursaspor forward opened the scoring after just 10 minutes, giving Nigeria an early advantage and demonstrating the confidence that has characterised his recent club performances.
>
> It was a significant moment for a player who had been absent from the Super Eagles since the 2025 Unity Cup final against Jamaica. His previous international goal had come against Zimbabwe in November 2023, making his strike against Russia a welcome return to the scoresheet for Nigeria.
>
> Iheanacho has been rebuilding his momentum in Turkey, where his prolific start to the season helped earn him a recall. His goalscoring form for Bursaspor had already strengthened the argument for his inclusion; Tuesday’s performance gave Chelle another reason to consider him seriously.
>
> Beyond the goal, his return offered Nigeria an experienced attacking option at a time when the squad contained several less-established players. His ability to finish with either foot and operate around the penalty area could prove valuable as the coach weighs up his forward options.
>
> After missing the recent AFCON qualifiers, Iheanacho has reminded the technical crew that he can still contribute at the international level.
>
> The challenge now is consistency. One goal cannot settle every question about his place in the team, but the forward has given Chelle a compelling reason to keep him in the conversation.

>
> Chelle’s substitutions helped turn the Game around
>
> When Russia moved 3-1 ahead in the 54th minute, Nigeria needed more than possession and hopeful attacks. They needed fresh energy, sharper movement and players capable of changing the momentum.
>
> And that response, exactly, was what Chelle’s substitutions helped deliver as Akor Adams entered at half-time. At the same time, Abdullahi Umar, Peter Edokpolor and Umar Abubakar were introduced as Nigeria searched for a way back into the match.
>
> The decisive breakthrough came in the 78th minute when Edokpolor scored on his senior international debut. His goal cut Russia’s lead to 3-2 and gave the Super Eagles a realistic target in the closing stages.
>
> Nigeria’s urgency increased, and Russia were forced to manage a contest that had appeared comfortable for the hosts for the best parts of the game earlier.
>
> The equaliser arrived deep into stoppage time. Emmanuel Fernandez helped initiate the counter-attack, Abdullahi Umar provided the assist, and Adams finished to complete Nigeria’s recovery.
>
> It was a timely reminder of the value of having attacking options who can influence a game from the bench. Adams supplied the finish, Umar delivered the decisive pass, and Edokpolor provided the spark that brought Nigeria back into contention.
>
> The draw also prevented Chelle from suffering consecutive defeats with the senior Super Eagles following the loss in Guinea-Bissau.
>
> However, the substitutions should be viewed alongside the wider performance. They helped rescue the result, but the coach will still need to address the issues that allowed Russia to take control in the first place.
>
> The newcomers gave Chelle fresh selection options
>

>

It's a unique 11-digit identity number issued by the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) that links all your bank accounts across different banks. Introduced in 2014, it helps reduce fraud and identify bank customers uniquely. Once you have a BVN, you can use it to open accounts at other banks — you don't need a new one.

turns.reply:
Inflation na when prices of goods and services dey generally rise over time. E mean say the same amount of money wey you fit use buy something before, e no go reach to buy am again.

Na like this e dey work: if ₦1,000 fit buy ten items last year, but this year e fit only buy five items, that one na inflation. The purchasing power of your money don reduce.

Things wey dey cause inflation fit be:
- Scarcity of goods (when demand pass supply)
- Increase in cost of production
- Too much money dey circulate
- Government policies

>

>
